### V-253391 · WN11-CC-000200 · CAT II: Administrator accounts must not be enumerated during elevation.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253391r958518_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000134-GPOS-00068 |
| Topic | Built-in & Privileged Account Hardening, Privilege Elevation (UAC / sudo) |
| CCI | CCI-001084 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-3 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | SC-3 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | SC-3 |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** Administrator accounts must not be enumerated during elevation.

**Why it matters:** Every computer comes with a few built-in "master" accounts whose names everyone knows. This rule makes those accounts harder to abuse, for example by not letting anyone log in directly as the master account and never allowing accounts with no password. It's like not leaving the master key labelled "MASTER KEY" hanging by the front door.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\CredUI | EnumerateAdministrators | REG_DWORD = 0 |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Credential User Interface | Enumerate administrator accounts on elevation | "Disabled" |

**How it works:** On Windows these are Security Options ('Accounts: Rename administrator account', 'Accounts: Guest account status', 'Accounts: Limit local account use of blank passwords to console logon only') plus LAPS for unique, rotated local administrator passwords.

**Also related (Privilege Elevation (UAC / sudo)):** UAC settings are Security Options named 'User Account Control: ...' (registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System: EnableLUA, ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin, ConsentPromptBehaviorUser, FilterAdministratorToken, EnableInstallerDetection, EnableSecureUIAPaths, EnableVirtualization).

**Operational impact:** Make sure at least one named administrator account with sudo or admin rights works before disabling root or Administrator logon paths. Renaming the built-in Administrator can break scripts that reference it by name.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\CredUI\

Value Name: EnumerateAdministrators

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Credential User Interface >> "Enumerate administrator accounts on elevation" to "Disabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Enumeration of administrator accounts when elevating can provide part of the logon information to an unauthorized user. This setting configures the system to always require users to type in a username and password to elevate a running application.

**Threat & control context:** Well-known accounts (root, Administrator, Guest) are guaranteed to exist with predictable names, which makes them ideal targets. Blocking direct logon forces attribution through named accounts (IA-2, AC-6(2)). Removing empty-password acceptance eliminates trivial access, and unique local admin passwords (LAPS) break pass-the-hash lateral movement across a fleet. Assess the effective result across every access path: console, SSH, RDP and network logon.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1078.001 Valid Accounts: Default Accounts; T1078.003 Valid Accounts: Local Accounts; T1110 Brute Force; T1548.002 Abuse Elevation Control: Bypass UAC; T1548.003 Abuse Elevation Control: Sudo and Sudo Caching; T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-001084**: Isolate security functions from nonsecurity functions.  
  Rev 5: SC-3 · Rev 4: SC-3 · Rev 3: SC-3

```text
If "Enhanced" level is enabled for telemetry, this must be configured. If "Security" or "Basic" are configured, this is NA. (See WN11-CC-000205).

If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection\

Value Name: LimitEnhancedDiagnosticDataWindowsAnalytics

Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000001 (1)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Data Collection and Preview Builds >> "Limit optional diagnostic data for Windows Analytics" to "Enabled" with "Enable Desktop Analytics collection" selected in "Options:".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Some features may communicate with the vendor, sending system information or downloading data or components for the feature. Limiting this capability will prevent potentially sensitive information from being sent outside the enterprise. The "Enhanced" level for telemetry includes additional information beyond "Security" and "Basic" on how Windows and apps are used and advanced reliability data. Windows Analytics can use a "limited enhanced" level to provide information such as health data for devices.

**Threat & control context:** Consumer-oriented and cloud-connected features can move government data (documents, typed input, location, diagnostic dumps containing memory contents) to vendor or third-party services outside the authorization boundary. Disabling or restricting them supports SC-7 (boundary protection), AC-20 (use of external systems), CM-7 and privacy controls, and removes unvetted functionality from the baseline.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service; T1213 Data from Information Repositories

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.  
  Rev 5: CM-6 b · Rev 4: CM-6 b · Rev 3: CM-6 b

### V-253393 · WN11-CC-000205 · CAT II: Windows Telemetry must not be configured to Full.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253393r1256676_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000205-GPOS-00083 |
| Topic | Telemetry, Cloud & Consumer Features |
| CCI | CCI-001312 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | SI-11 a |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | SI-11 a |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | SI-11 b |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** Windows Telemetry must not be configured to Full.

**Why it matters:** Modern computers like to "phone home", sending usage data to the manufacturer, syncing to personal cloud accounts, or showing ads and suggestions. This rule turns those features off or down so government information stays inside the government's systems, like not letting a delivery driver wander through the office and take notes.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection | AllowTelemetry | REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0) (Security) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Data Collection and Preview Builds | Allow Diagnostic Data | "Enabled" with "Send required diagnostic data" selected in "Options:" |

**How it works:** On Windows these are mostly Administrative Templates under Windows Components (Data Collection and Preview Builds, Cloud Content, Search, Store, OneDrive, Windows Error Reporting, App Privacy) and the Microsoft Edge templates. Verify the registry values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\... as shown in each check.

**Operational impact:** Users lose consumer conveniences such as Store apps, Microsoft-account sign-in and web results in search. Enterprise management may need a minimum telemetry level (e.g. for Windows Update for Business reports), so align the value with the STIG's allowed options.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection\

Value Name: AllowTelemetry

Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000000 (0) (Security)
0x00000001 (1) (Basic)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Data Collection and Preview Builds >> "Allow Diagnostic Data" to "Enabled" with "Send required diagnostic data" selected in "Options:".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Some features may communicate with the vendor, sending system information or downloading data or components for the feature. Limiting this capability will prevent potentially sensitive information from being sent outside the enterprise.

The "Security" option for Telemetry configures the lowest amount of data, effectively none outside of the Malicious Software Removal Tool (MSRT), Defender, and telemetry client settings.

"Basic" sends basic diagnostic and usage data and may be required to support some Microsoft services.

"Enhanced" includes additional information on how Windows and apps are used and advanced reliability data. Windows Analytics can use a "limited enhanced" level to provide information such as health data for devices.

**Threat & control context:** Consumer-oriented and cloud-connected features can move government data (documents, typed input, location, diagnostic dumps containing memory contents) to vendor or third-party services outside the authorization boundary. Disabling or restricting them supports SC-7 (boundary protection), AC-20 (use of external systems), CM-7 and privacy controls, and removes unvetted functionality from the baseline.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service; T1213 Data from Information Repositories

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-001312**: Generate error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited.  
  Rev 5: SI-11 a · Rev 4: SI-11 a · Rev 3: SI-11 b

### V-253394 · WN11-CC-000206 · CAT III: Windows Update must not obtain updates from other PCs on the internet.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253394r1268251_rule` |
| Severity | CAT III (low) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000480-GPOS-00227 |
| Topic | Patching & Supported Software |
| CCI | CCI-000366 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | CM-6 b |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** Windows Update must not obtain updates from other PCs on the internet.

**Why it matters:** Software makers regularly release fixes for security holes they discover. This rule requires installing those fixes and only running versions that are still supported. It's like getting the recall repair on your car: skip it, and the known problem stays there for anyone to take advantage of.

**How important is it?** Low priority (CAT III): This setting adds an extra layer of protection. A gap here on its own is less likely to cause harm, but it weakens the overall defenses.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\DeliveryOptimization\Config | DODownloadMode | REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0) - Off |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Delivery Optimization | Download Mode | "Enabled" with any option except "Internet" selected |

**How it works:** On Windows, patch through WSUS, ConfigMgr, Intune or Windows Update for Business. Check installed updates with 'Get-HotFix' and the OS build with 'winver' against Microsoft's lifecycle page.

**Operational impact:** Patching requires maintenance windows and sometimes reboots. Test critical applications against updates in a staging environment, but don't let testing stretch beyond IAVM deadlines.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeliveryOptimization\

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000000 (0) - No peering (HTTP Only)
0x00000001 (1) - Peers on same NAT only (LAN)
0x00000002 (2) - Local Network / Private group peering (Group)
0x00000063 (99) - Simple download mode, no peering (Simple)
0x00000064 (100) - Bypass mode, Delivery Optimization not used (Bypass)

A value of 0x00000003 (3), Internet, is a finding.

Standalone systems (configured in Settings):

If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\DeliveryOptimization\Config\

Value Name: DODownloadMode

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000000 (0) - Off
0x00000001 (1) - LAN
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Delivery Optimization >> "Download Mode" to "Enabled" with any option except "Internet" selected.

Acceptable selections include:
Bypass (100)
Group (2)
HTTP only (0)
LAN (1)
Simple (99)
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Windows 11 allows Windows Update to obtain updates from additional sources instead of Microsoft. In addition to Microsoft, updates can be obtained from and sent to PCs on the local network as well as on the internet. This is part of the Windows Update trusted process; however, to minimize outside exposure, obtaining updates from or sending to systems on the internet must be prevented.

**Threat & control context:** Known, unpatched vulnerabilities remain the most common initial-access and privilege-escalation vector. Running an unsupported release means new vulnerabilities will never be fixed. SI-2 (flaw remediation) and SA-22 (unsupported system components) require timely patching per organizational timelines (IAVM compliance in DoD) and replacement of end-of-life components. Unsupported OS findings are CAT I because they can't be mitigated by configuration alone.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application; T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation; T1210 Exploitation of Remote Services

**Severity rationale:** CAT III: any vulnerability whose existence degrades measures to protect against loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.  
  Rev 5: CM-6 b · Rev 4: CM-6 b · Rev 3: CM-6 b

### V-253395 · WN11-CC-000210 · CAT II: The Microsoft Defender SmartScreen for Explorer must be enabled.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253395r958478_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000095-GPOS-00049 |
| Topic | Anti-Malware & Reputation Protection, System Services & Daemons |
| CCI | CCI-000381 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-7 a |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | CM-7 a |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | CM-7 |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** The Microsoft Defender SmartScreen for Explorer must be enabled.

**Why it matters:** This keeps the computer's virus scanner switched on and up to date, and warns people before they open files or websites known to be dangerous. It's the digital equivalent of a smoke detector with fresh batteries.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System | EnableSmartScreen | REG_DWORD = 0x00000001 (1) |
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System | ShellSmartScreenLevel | REG_SZ = Block |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> File Explorer | Configure Windows Defender SmartScreen | "Enabled" with "Warn and prevent bypass" selected |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Defender SmartScreen | Explorer |  |

**How it works:** On Windows, configure Microsoft Defender Antivirus under Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Microsoft Defender Antivirus, and SmartScreen under Windows Components >> File Explorer and Microsoft Edge. Verify with 'Get-MpComputerStatus' (AMServiceEnabled, AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated). If a third-party DoD-approved product is deployed, Defender may run in passive mode.

**Also related (System Services & Daemons):** On Windows, set the service startup type through Group Policy (System Services) or 'Set-Service -StartupType Disabled'. Check with 'Get-Service <name> | Select Status, StartType'.

**Operational impact:** Real-time scanning adds I/O overhead. Define vetted exclusions for databases and build directories only with ISSO approval and document them.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
This is applicable to unclassified systems, for other systems this is NA.

If the following registry values do not exist or are not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System\

Value Name: EnableSmartScreen

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000001 (1)

And

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System\

Value Name: ShellSmartScreenLevel

Value Type: REG_SZ
Value: Block
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> File Explorer >> "Configure Windows Defender SmartScreen" to "Enabled" with "Warn and prevent bypass" selected.

Windows 11 includes duplicate policies for this setting. It can also be configured under Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Defender SmartScreen >> Explorer.
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Microsoft Defender SmartScreen helps protect systems from programs downloaded from the internet that may be malicious. Enabling Microsoft Defender SmartScreen will warn or prevent users from running potentially malicious programs.

**Threat & control context:** Signature and behavioral anti-malware, together with reputation services such as SmartScreen, address commodity and opportunistic threats at the endpoint (SI-3 malicious code protection, SI-3(2) automatic updates). DoD typically requires an approved enterprise endpoint-security suite. The STIG check confirms that a capable product is installed, running and updating, and that users can't bypass warnings.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1562.001 Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools; T1204 User Execution; T1566 Phishing; T1543 Create or Modify System Process; T1210 Exploitation of Remote Services

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000381**: Configure the system to provide only organization-defined mission essential capabilities.  
  Rev 5: CM-7 a · Rev 4: CM-7 a · Rev 3: CM-7

### V-253396 · WN11-CC-000215 · CAT II: Explorer Data Execution Prevention must be enabled.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253396r958928_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000433-GPOS-00192 |
| Topic | Kernel & Memory Exploit Mitigations, System Services & Daemons |
| CCI | CCI-002824 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | SI-16 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | SI-16 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | n/a |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** Explorer Data Execution Prevention must be enabled.

**Why it matters:** Hackers often break in by tricking a program into running their own instructions. These settings turn on built-in defenses that shuffle where things sit in memory and refuse to run code from places it shouldn't come from. It's like a bank regularly moving the vault around and refusing to accept instructions written on deposit slips.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *DEP*: Data Execution Prevention: stops programs running code from memory areas meant only for data.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer | NoDataExecutionPrevention | REG_DWORD = 0 (or if the Value Name does not exist) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> File Explorer | Turn off Data Execution Prevention for Explorer | "Not Configured" or "Disabled" |

**How it works:** On Windows, set these through Exploit Protection (system DEP, SEHOP, ASLR: 'Get-ProcessMitigation -System'), the 'Turn On Virtualization Based Security' policy under Device Guard, and the MS Security Guide 'Enable Structured Exception Handling Overwrite Protection (SEHOP)' policy.

**Also related (System Services & Daemons):** On Windows, set the service startup type through Group Policy (System Services) or 'Set-Service -StartupType Disabled'. Check with 'Get-Service <name> | Select Status, StartType'.

**Operational impact:** Restricting ptrace and dmesg affects debuggers (gdb, strace) for non-root users. Disabling core dumps removes crash diagnostics. HVCI can block older or unsigned drivers, so check driver compatibility first. Most sysctl changes are immediate, while boot parameters require a reboot.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
The default behavior is for data execution prevention to be turned on for file explorer.

If it exists and is configured with a value of "1", this is a finding.

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer\

Value Name: NoDataExecutionPrevention

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0 (or if the Value Name does not exist)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
The default behavior is for data execution prevention to be turned on for file explorer.

To correct this, configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> File Explorer >> "Turn off Data Execution Prevention for Explorer" to "Not Configured" or "Disabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Data Execution Prevention (DEP) provides additional protection by performing checks on memory to help prevent malicious code from running. This setting will prevent Data Execution Prevention from being turned off for File Explorer.

**Threat & control context:** These mitigations don't remove vulnerabilities. They raise the cost and lower the reliability of exploiting them. ASLR, DEP/NX and SEHOP break classic memory-corruption techniques. Restricting ptrace, kernel pointer exposure, dmesg, unprivileged BPF and kexec removes common local-privilege-escalation primitives and information leaks. Hypervisor-enforced code integrity (HVCI) and VBS protect the kernel itself. These support SI-16 (memory protection), SC-39 (process isolation) and CM-6 baseline configuration.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation; T1055 Process Injection; T1014 Rootkit; T1203 Exploitation for Client Execution; T1543 Create or Modify System Process; T1210 Exploitation of Remote Services

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-002824**: Implement organization-defined controls to protect the system memory from unauthorized code execution.  
  Rev 5: SI-16 · Rev 4: SI-16 · Rev 3: n/a

---

### V-253398 · WN11-CC-000225 · CAT II: File Explorer shell protocol must run in protected mode.

| Field | Value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** File Explorer shell protocol must run in protected mode.

**Why it matters:** This is one of the many "house rules" that together make the computer harder to break into. On its own it might close only a small gap, but hundreds of small gaps closed together make a big difference, like checking every window in the house is shut, not just the front door.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer | PreXPSP2ShellProtocolBehavior | REG_DWORD = 0 (or if the Value Name does not exist) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> File Explorer | Turn off shell protocol protected mode | "Not Configured" or "Disabled" |

**How it works:** Apply the change through Group Policy where possible (the DISA STIG GPO package provides importable GPOs) rather than editing the registry by hand, so it is enforced and auditable. Confirm with the check procedure and 'gpresult /h'.

**Operational impact:** Test in a non-production environment first and record any functional impact. If the setting can't be applied, document the deviation and its mitigation with the ISSO.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
The default behavior is for shell protected mode to be turned on for file explorer.

If it exists and is configured with a value of "1", this is a finding.

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer\

Value Name: PreXPSP2ShellProtocolBehavior

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0 (or if the Value Name does not exist)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
The default behavior is for shell protected mode to be turned on for file explorer.

To correct this, configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> File Explorer >> "Turn off shell protocol protected mode" to "Not Configured" or "Disabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** The shell protocol will limit the set of folders applications can open when run in protected mode. Restricting files an application can open, to a limited set of folders, increases the security of Windows.

**Threat & control context:** This requirement is part of the secure configuration baseline (CM-6 configuration settings, with CM-7 least functionality where applicable). Individually it may close a narrow weakness. Collectively, baseline settings remove the default-insecure states that attackers rely on, and deviations must be documented and risk-accepted in the system's POA&M or as an approved exception.

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.

### V-253399 · WN11-CC-000252 · CAT II: Windows 11 must be configured to disable Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253399r1259989_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000095-GPOS-00049 |
| Topic | Network Stack Hardening, Telemetry, Cloud & Consumer Features |
| CCI | CCI-000381 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-7 a |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | CM-7 a |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | CM-7 |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer must be configured to disable Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting.

**Why it matters:** These settings change how the computer handles network traffic at a low level, for example ignoring suspicious "take a detour" messages and not answering "who is this?" broadcasts that attackers can fake. It's like a mail room that refuses packages with forged return addresses and won't hand mail to anyone who just shouts a name.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *Group Policy*: The central way Windows administrators push settings to many computers at once.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\PolicyManager\current\device\ApplicationManagement  (For Intune-managed systems) | AllowGameDVR | REG_DWORD = 0x00000000 (0) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting | Enables or disables Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting | "Disabled" |

**How it works:** On Windows, set these through MSS (Legacy) templates included with the STIG GPO package (DisableIPSourceRouting, EnableICMPRedirect, NoNameReleaseOnDemand) and Network >> DNS Client >> 'Turn off multicast name resolution' (EnableMulticast = 0). Hardened UNC Paths requires mutual authentication and integrity for \\*\SYSVOL and \\*\NETLOGON.

**Also related (Telemetry, Cloud & Consumer Features):** On Windows these are mostly Administrative Templates under Windows Components (Data Collection and Preview Builds, Cloud Content, Search, Store, OneDrive, Windows Error Reporting, App Privacy) and the Microsoft Edge templates. Verify the registry values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\... as shown in each check.

**Operational impact:** Hosts that legitimately route (VPN concentrators, container and Kubernetes nodes, libvirt hosts) need IP forwarding and must document the exception. Disabling LLMNR and NetBIOS requires working DNS for all name lookups.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
This is NA for Windows 11 LTSC.

If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\GameDVR\  (For GPO-managed systems)
Or
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\PolicyManager\current\device\ApplicationManagement  (For Intune-managed systems)

Value Name: AllowGameDVR

Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0x00000000 (0)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
For GPO-managed systems:
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting >> "Enables or disables Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting" to "Disabled".

For Intune-managed systems:
Revise the Intune policy to disable Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting.
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting is intended for use with games; however, it could record screenshots of other applications and expose sensitive data. Disabling the feature will prevent this from occurring.

Note: A different registry location is needed when systems are managed by Intune versus GPO.

**Threat & control context:** Host network-stack defaults favor interoperability over safety. Accepting ICMP redirects or source-routed packets lets an on-path attacker reroute traffic. IP forwarding turns a host into an unintended router between security zones. Multicast name resolution (LLMNR, NBT-NS, mDNS) is trivially poisoned to capture NTLM hashes. Reverse-path filtering and SYN cookies blunt spoofing and resource-exhaustion attacks. These settings support SC-5, SC-7 (boundary protection) and CM-7.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1557 Adversary-in-the-Middle; T1557.001 LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay; T1040 Network Sniffing; T1498 Network Denial of Service; T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service; T1213 Data from Information Repositories

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000381**: Configure the system to provide only organization-defined mission essential capabilities.  
  Rev 5: CM-7 a · Rev 4: CM-7 a · Rev 3: CM-7

### V-253400 · WN11-CC-000255 · CAT II: The use of a hardware security device with Windows Hello for Business must be enabled.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253400r1268251_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000480-GPOS-00227 |
| Topic | Logon Screen & Desktop Settings, System Services & Daemons |
| CCI | CCI-000366 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | CM-6 b |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** The use of a hardware security device with Windows Hello for Business must be enabled.

**Why it matters:** This decides what the sign-in screen shows and which shortcuts are allowed. For example, it hides the list of usernames, doesn't show who signed in last, and turns off "sign in automatically". It's like a hotel front desk that won't tell a stranger which room a guest is in.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\PassportForWork | RequireSecurityDevice | REG_DWORD = 1 |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Hello for Business | Use a hardware security device | "Enabled" |

**How it works:** On Windows, use Security Options such as 'Interactive logon: Don't display last signed-in' and 'Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL' (Disabled). Administrative Templates >> System >> Logon covers enumerating local users, convenience PIN and picture password. Credential User Interface >> 'Do not display the password reveal button' handles the reveal button.

**Also related (System Services & Daemons):** On Windows, set the service startup type through Group Policy (System Services) or 'Set-Service -StartupType Disabled'. Check with 'Get-Service <name> | Select Status, StartType'.

**Operational impact:** Users will need to type their username in full and can't use convenience sign-in methods. Hiding restart buttons on the logon screen means console users need credentials to reboot.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
Virtual desktop implementations currently may not support the use of TPMs. For virtual desktop implementations where the virtual desktop instance is deleted or refreshed upon logoff, this is NA.

If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\PassportForWork\

Value Name: RequireSecurityDevice

Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 1
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Hello for Business >> "Use a hardware security device" to "Enabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** The use of a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) to store keys for Windows Hello for Business provides additional security. Keys stored in the TPM may only be used on that system while keys stored using software are more susceptible to compromise and could be used on other systems.

**Threat & control context:** The logon surface can leak information (usernames, the last logged-on user, local administrator lists) that cuts an attacker's effort in half, and convenience features (automatic logon, picture passwords, convenience PINs, password reveal buttons) weaken authentication assurance. These settings reduce information disclosure (AC-14, IA-6 authenticator feedback) and keep interactive logon on approved authenticators.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1087 Account Discovery; T1078 Valid Accounts; T1543 Create or Modify System Process; T1210 Exploitation of Remote Services

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.  
  Rev 5: CM-6 b · Rev 4: CM-6 b · Rev 3: CM-6 b

### V-253401 · WN11-CC-000260 · CAT II: Windows 11 must be configured to require a minimum PIN length of six characters or greater.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253401r1268251_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000480-GPOS-00227 |
| Topic | Password Strength & Complexity |
| CCI | CCI-000366 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | CM-6 b |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** This computer must be configured to require a minimum PIN length of six characters or greater.

**Why it matters:** This sets the rules for how strong a password must be: long enough, and mixing capitals, lowercase letters, numbers and symbols. Short or simple passwords can be guessed by computers in seconds. A long, varied password is like a key with many unique notches that's much harder to copy.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *Group Policy*: The central way Windows administrators push settings to many computers at once.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Policies\PassportForWork\[guid]\device\policies\PINComplexity  (For Intune-managed systems) | MinimumPINLength | REG_DWORD = 6 (or greater) |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> System >> PIN Complexity | Minimum PIN length | "6" or greater |

**How it works:** Windows sets this in Account Policies >> Password Policy ('Minimum password length', 'Password must meet complexity requirements'). Domain-wide values come from the Default Domain Policy or Fine-Grained Password Policies (PSOs). Lengths above 14 require the 'Relax minimum password length limits' setting on newer builds.

**Operational impact:** Takes effect at each user's next password change. Communicate the new requirements beforehand, and check that provisioning scripts and self-service reset portals can generate compliant passwords.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\PassportForWork\PINComplexity\  (For GPO-managed systems)
Or
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Policies\PassportForWork\[guid]\device\policies\PINComplexity  (For Intune-managed systems)

Value Name: MinimumPINLength

Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 6 (or greater)
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
For GPO-managed systems:

Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> System >> PIN Complexity >> "Minimum PIN length" to "6" or greater.

For Intune-managed systems:

Revise the Intune policy to set the minimum PIN length to "6" or greater.
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Windows allows the use of PINs and biometrics for authentication without sending a password to a network or website where it could be compromised. Longer minimum PIN lengths increase the available combinations an attacker would have to attempt. Shorter minimum length significantly reduces the strength.

Note: A different registry location is needed when systems are managed by Intune versus GPO.

**Threat & control context:** Length and composition rules raise the cost of both online guessing and offline cracking of captured hashes (IA-5(1)). DoD still requires a 15-character minimum with character-class rules, while NIST SP 800-63B now favors length plus breached-password screening over composition rules. Where the two conflict, the STIG governs for DoD systems. Note that complexity rules apply only when a password is changed, so assess the age of existing passwords too.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1110.002 Brute Force: Password Cracking; T1110.001 Brute Force: Password Guessing

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.  
  Rev 5: CM-6 b · Rev 4: CM-6 b · Rev 3: CM-6 b

### V-253402 · WN11-CC-000270 · CAT II: Passwords must not be saved in the Remote Desktop Client.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253402r1051051_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000373-GPOS-00156 |
| Topic | Remote Desktop & Remote Management |
| CCI | CCI-002038 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-11 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | IA-11 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | n/a |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** Passwords must not be saved in the Remote Desktop Client.

**Why it matters:** Administrators can control computers from far away, as if they were sitting at the keyboard. This rule makes sure those remote connections are encrypted, require a proper sign-in every time, and can't be used to copy files around carelessly. It's like requiring a video-verified, recorded call before anyone can give orders over the phone.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *Remote Desktop (RDP)*: A way to see and control a Windows computer's screen from another computer.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services | DisablePasswordSaving | REG_DWORD = 1 |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Remote Desktop Services >> Remote Desktop Connection Client | Do not allow passwords | be saved" to "Enabled" |

**How it works:** On Windows, RDP settings are under Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Remote Desktop Services >> Remote Desktop Session Host (Security / Device and Resource Redirection / Session Time Limits), and WinRM settings under Windows Components >> Windows Remote Management (WinRM Client / WinRM Service). Verify WinRM with 'winrm get winrm/config'.

**Operational impact:** Disabling drive and clipboard redirection affects admin convenience. WinRM restrictions can break management tools that use Basic auth over HTTP (some older configuration-management and monitoring products), so move those to Kerberos or HTTPS.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\

Value Name: DisablePasswordSaving

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 1
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Remote Desktop Services >> Remote Desktop Connection Client >> "Do not allow passwords to be saved" to "Enabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Saving passwords in the Remote Desktop Client could allow an unauthorized user to establish a remote desktop session to another system. The system must be configured to prevent users from saving passwords in the Remote Desktop Client.

**Threat & control context:** Remote-management protocols give interactive or programmatic control of a host and are a favored vector for both ransomware operators and insiders. Requirements include encrypted transport, no Basic/Digest authentication or unencrypted WinRM traffic, always prompting for credentials, no saved RDP passwords, no drive redirection, and session time limits. These implement AC-17 (remote access), AC-17(2) (confidentiality and integrity via encryption), SC-8 and AC-12 (session termination).

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol; T1021.006 Remote Services: Windows Remote Management; T1563 Remote Service Session Hijacking; T1040 Network Sniffing

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-002038**: The organization requires users to reauthenticate upon organization-defined circumstances or situations requiring reauthentication.  
  Rev 5: IA-11 · Rev 4: IA-11 · Rev 3: n/a

**Operational impact:** Disabling drive and clipboard redirection affects admin convenience. WinRM restrictions can break management tools that use Basic auth over HTTP (some older configuration-management and monitoring products), so move those to Kerberos or HTTPS.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\

Value Name: MinEncryptionLevel

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 3
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Remote Desktop Services >> Remote Desktop Session Host >> Security >> "Set client connection encryption level" to "Enabled" and "High Level".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Remote connections must be encrypted to prevent interception of data or sensitive information. Selecting "High Level" will ensure encryption of Remote Desktop Services sessions in both directions.

**Threat & control context:** Remote-management protocols give interactive or programmatic control of a host and are a favored vector for both ransomware operators and insiders. Requirements include encrypted transport, no Basic/Digest authentication or unencrypted WinRM traffic, always prompting for credentials, no saved RDP passwords, no drive redirection, and session time limits. These implement AC-17 (remote access), AC-17(2) (confidentiality and integrity via encryption), SC-8 and AC-12 (session termination).

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol; T1021.006 Remote Services: Windows Remote Management; T1563 Remote Service Session Hijacking; T1040 Network Sniffing

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000068**: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality of remote access sessions.  
  Rev 5: AC-17 (2) · Rev 4: AC-17 (2) · Rev 3: AC-17 (2)

This rule turns those features off or down so government information stays inside the government's systems, like not letting a delivery driver wander through the office and take notes.

Verify the registry values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\... as shown in each check.


#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Threat & control context:** Consumer-oriented and cloud-connected features can move government data (documents, typed input, location, diagnostic dumps containing memory contents) to vendor or third-party services outside the authorization boundary. Disabling or restricting them supports SC-7 (boundary protection), AC-20 (use of external systems), CM-7 and privacy controls, and removes unvetted functionality from the baseline.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service; T1213 Data from Information Repositories

### V-253410 · WN11-CC-000310 · CAT II: Users must be prevented from changing installation options.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253410r1051053_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000362-GPOS-00149 |
| Topic | Privilege Elevation (UAC / sudo) |
| CCI | CCI-003980, CCI-001812 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-11 (2) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | CM-11 (2) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | n/a |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** Users must be prevented from changing installation options.

**Why it matters:** Even administrators work day-to-day without full power, and the system asks them to confirm, often by re-entering a password, before doing anything that could change important settings. That way, a harmful program can't quietly use admin power behind their back. It's like a bank requiring a second signature for large withdrawals.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer | EnableUserControl | REG_DWORD = 0 |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Installer | Allow user control over installs | "Disabled" |

**How it works:** UAC settings are Security Options named 'User Account Control: ...' (registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System: EnableLUA, ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin, ConsentPromptBehaviorUser, FilterAdministratorToken, EnableInstallerDetection, EnableSecureUIAPaths, EnableVirtualization).

**Operational impact:** Turning off password-less sudo affects automation such as Ansible and cron jobs. Use dedicated automation accounts with tightly scoped command lists and documented exceptions. Disabling UAC (EnableLUA = 0) is not acceptable and also breaks Store/UWP apps.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer\

Value Name: EnableUserControl

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Installer >> "Allow user control over installs" to "Disabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Installation options for applications are typically controlled by administrators. This setting prevents users from changing installation options that may bypass security features.

**Threat & control context:** Elevation controls make privilege use deliberate, authenticated and auditable (AC-6(1)/(2)/(9)/(10), IA-11 re-authentication). UAC's secure-desktop prompt resists UI spoofing and input injection by malware running in the user's session. sudo restrictions (no NOPASSWD, no '!authenticate', short timestamp_timeout, no blanket ALL grants) prevent silent escalation by any process running as an admin user. Every elevation event should produce an audit record.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1548.002 Abuse Elevation Control: Bypass UAC; T1548.003 Abuse Elevation Control: Sudo and Sudo Caching; T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-003980**: Allow user installation of software only with explicit privileged status.  
  Rev 5: CM-11 (2) · Rev 4: n/a · Rev 3: n/a
- **CCI-001812**: The information system prohibits user installation of software without explicit privileged status.  
  Rev 5: n/a · Rev 4: CM-11 (2) · Rev 3: n/a

### V-253413 · WN11-CC-000325 · CAT II: Automatically signing in the last interactive user after a system-initiated restart must be disabled.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253413r991591_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000480-GPOS-00229 |
| Topic | File Sharing (SMB) & Anonymous Access |
| CCI | CCI-000366 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | CM-6 b |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | CM-6 b |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** Automatically signing in the last interactive user after a system-initiated restart must be disabled.

**Why it matters:** Computers on a network share files with each other using a system called SMB. This rule makes every file-sharing conversation carry a tamper-proof "seal" and stops strangers who haven't signed in from browsing the list of users and shared folders. It's like requiring visitors to sign in at the front desk before they can read the staff directory.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System | DisableAutomaticRestartSignOn | REG_DWORD = 1 |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Logon Options | Sign-in last interactive user automatically after a system-initiated restart | "Disabled" |

**How it works:** Mostly Security Options: 'Microsoft network client/server: Digitally sign communications (always)' (RequireSecuritySignature), 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' (RestrictAnonymous), 'Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users', 'Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares', 'Network access: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM'. SMBv1 is removed with 'Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol'. Check with 'Get-SmbServerConfiguration'.

**Operational impact:** Mandatory signing adds CPU overhead on high-throughput file servers (usually negligible on modern hardware) and can break very old clients and some NAS devices. Restricting anonymous access can affect legacy apps that rely on null sessions.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\

Value Name: DisableAutomaticRestartSignOn

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 1
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Logon Options >> "Sign-in last interactive user automatically after a system-initiated restart" to "Disabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Windows can be configured to automatically sign the user back in after a Windows Update restart. Some protections are in place to help ensure this is done in a secure fashion; however, disabling this will prevent the caching of credentials for this purpose and also ensure the user is aware of the restart.

**Threat & control context:** SMB is the backbone of Windows file and administrative traffic and a principal lateral-movement channel. Unsigned SMB enables NTLM relay attacks. Anonymous (null session) access and SAM/share enumeration give unauthenticated attackers reconnaissance data such as user lists and group memberships. SMBv1 lacks modern protections and was the propagation vector for WannaCry and NotPetya. These settings support AC-3, AC-14 (actions without identification), SC-8 and CM-7.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1557.001 LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay; T1135 Network Share Discovery; T1087 Account Discovery; T1021.002 Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000366**: Implement the security configuration settings.  
  Rev 5: CM-6 b · Rev 4: CM-6 b · Rev 3: CM-6 b

### V-253414 · WN11-CC-000326 · CAT II: PowerShell script block logging must be enabled on Windows 11.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253414r958422_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000042-GPOS-00020 |
| Topic | PowerShell & Scripting Security, System Services & Daemons |
| CCI | CCI-000135 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | AU-3 (1) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | AU-3 (1) |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | AU-3 (1) |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** PowerShell script block logging must be enabled on this computer.

**Why it matters:** PowerShell is a powerful tool for automating tasks on Windows, which also makes it a favorite of hackers. This rule makes the computer keep a detailed record of every PowerShell command that runs, like a CCTV camera pointed at the most powerful tool in the workshop.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *PowerShell*: A powerful Windows command-line and scripting tool.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging | EnableScriptBlockLogging | REG_DWORD = 1 |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows PowerShell | Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging | "Enabled" |

**How it works:** On Windows, configure these under Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows PowerShell: 'Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging' (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging EnableScriptBlockLogging = 1) and 'Turn on PowerShell Transcription'. Logs go to Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational. Write transcripts to a protected, centrally collected location.

**Also related (System Services & Daemons):** On Windows, set the service startup type through Group Policy (System Services) or 'Set-Service -StartupType Disabled'. Check with 'Get-Service <name> | Select Status, StartType'.

**Operational impact:** Script-block logs can be large and may capture secrets embedded in scripts. Size the PowerShell Operational log appropriately and restrict who can read it.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging\

Value Name: EnableScriptBlockLogging

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 1
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows PowerShell >> "Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging" to "Enabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Maintaining an audit trail of system activity logs can help identify configuration errors, troubleshoot service disruptions, and analyze compromises that have occurred, as well as detect attacks. Audit logs are necessary to provide a trail of evidence in case the system or network is compromised. Collecting this data is essential for analyzing the security of information assets and detecting signs of suspicious and unexpected behavior.

Enabling PowerShell script block logging will record detailed information from the processing of PowerShell commands and scripts. This can provide additional detail when malware has run on a system.

**Threat & control context:** PowerShell is the dominant 'living off the land' tool in Windows intrusions. Script Block Logging (event 4104) records de-obfuscated code as it executes, and Transcription records full session input and output. Together they provide high-fidelity detection content for AU-2/AU-12 and SI-4. Removing PowerShell 2.0 prevents downgrade attacks that bypass these logs and AMSI.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell; T1059.005 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic; T1562.003 Impair Defenses: Impair Command History Logging; T1543 Create or Modify System Process; T1210 Exploitation of Remote Services

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000135**: Generate audit records containing the organization-defined additional information that is to be included in the audit records.  
  Rev 5: AU-3 (1) · Rev 4: AU-3 (1) · Rev 3: AU-3 (1)

### V-253415 · WN11-CC-000327 · CAT II: PowerShell Transcription must be enabled on Windows 11.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253415r1259992_rule` |
| Severity | CAT II (medium) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000041-GPOS-00019 |
| Topic | PowerShell & Scripting Security, System Services & Daemons |
| CCI | CCI-000134 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | AU-3 e |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | AU-3 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | AU-3 |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** PowerShell Transcription must be enabled on this computer.

**Why it matters:** PowerShell is a powerful tool for automating tasks on Windows, which also makes it a favorite of hackers. This rule makes the computer keep a detailed record of every PowerShell command that runs, like a CCTV camera pointed at the most powerful tool in the workshop.

**How important is it?** Medium priority (CAT II): If this setting is wrong, it could help an attacker gain access, cause damage, or hide what they did. Most rules fall into this category.

**Key terms:**
- *Registry*: Windows' internal database of settings.
- *PowerShell*: A powerful Windows command-line and scripting tool.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\Transcription | EnableTranscripting | REG_DWORD = 1 |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows PowerShell | Turn on PowerShell Transcription | "Enabled" |

**How it works:** On Windows, configure these under Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows PowerShell: 'Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging' (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging EnableScriptBlockLogging = 1) and 'Turn on PowerShell Transcription'. Logs go to Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational. Write transcripts to a protected, centrally collected location.

**Also related (System Services & Daemons):** On Windows, set the service startup type through Group Policy (System Services) or 'Set-Service -StartupType Disabled'. Check with 'Get-Service <name> | Select Status, StartType'.

**Operational impact:** Script-block logs can be large and may capture secrets embedded in scripts. Size the PowerShell Operational log appropriately and restrict who can read it.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\Transcription\

Value Name: EnableTranscripting

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 1

The location used for log storage must be a write-only, restricted directory (preferably a network share) that security personnel can access. The registry value setting for "Transcript output directory" is set by the GPO to "C:\ProgramData\PS_Transcript". That directory allows Read, Modify, and Delete access by standard (nonprivileged) user accounts. Either a different directory that has appropriate access permissions must be configured (see Fix text), or the permissions for the existing Transcript output directory must be configured appropriately.

If the directory used to store the PowerShell transcription log files (Transcript output directory) permits read or modify access by nonprivileged users, this is a finding.

If the output directory set by the GPO is preferred, the access permissions must be revised to ensure the PowerShell Transcription log files are accessible only to the Administrator and System accounts.

To review permissions of the output directory, enter the following commands.
Open "Command Prompt (Admin)".

[Enter "icacls" followed by the directory configured to store PowerShell Transcription logs:]
icacls C:\ProgramData\PS_Transcript

If log files currently reside in the output directory, issue the following:
icacls C:\ProgramData\PS_Transcript\*.*

The results must be displayed as below:
NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(OI)(CI)(IO)(F)
BUILTIN\Administrators:(OI)(CI)(IO)(F)
*NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users:(OI)(CI)(WD,AD)
*BUILTIN\Users:(OI)(CI)(WD,AD)
*Note: The standard user accounts may differ based on the system's purpose/role and Active Directory structure.

If the directory used to store PowerShell Transcription logs is not configured to provide Full Control access to Administrative and System accounts while permitting write-only access for standard user accounts, this is a finding.
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows PowerShell >> "Turn on PowerShell Transcription" to "Enabled".

If a centralized (versus local) Transcript output directory is preferred, configure the Transcript output directory to point to a Central Log Server or another secure location to prevent user Read, Modify, and Delete access by nonprivileged accounts.

Ensure the selected directory is write-only with Full Control access granted to Administrator and System accounts.

Enter the following registry value:
Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\Transcription
*Value Name: OutputDirectory
Value Type: REG_SZ (String Value)

* Note: "OutputDirectory" value should be: "[custom directory path (e.g., I:\UserX_PowerShellTranscripts)]"

If the folder configured (in the registry) as the Transcript output directory is not configured to provide Full Control access to Administrative and System accounts, while permitting WD, AD access for standard user accounts, issue the following commands:
Open "Command Prompt (Admin)".
1. If the directory configured to store PowerShell Transcription logs does not exist:
mkdir C:\ProgramData\PS_Transcript
2. Assign appropriate permissions to Administrators group and System account:
icacls "C:\ProgramData\PS_Transcript" /inheritance:r /grant:r "Administrators:(OI)(CI)(F)" /grant:r "SYSTEM":(OI)(CI)(F)
3. Assign appropriate permissions to user groups:
icacls "C:\ProgramData\PS_Transcript" /grant:r "Users":(OI)(CI)(WD,AD) /t /c
icacls "C:\ProgramData\PS_Transcript" /grant:r "Authenticated Users":(OI)(CI)(WD,AD) /t /c
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Maintaining an audit trail of system activity logs can help identify configuration errors, troubleshoot service disruptions, and analyze compromises that have occurred, as well as detect attacks. Audit logs are necessary to provide a trail of evidence in case the system or network is compromised. Collecting this data is essential for analyzing the security of information assets and detecting signs of suspicious and unexpected behavior.

Enabling PowerShell Transcription will record detailed information from the processing of PowerShell commands and scripts. This can provide additional detail when malware has run on a system.

**Threat & control context:** PowerShell is the dominant 'living off the land' tool in Windows intrusions. Script Block Logging (event 4104) records de-obfuscated code as it executes, and Transcription records full session input and output. Together they provide high-fidelity detection content for AU-2/AU-12 and SI-4. Removing PowerShell 2.0 prevents downgrade attacks that bypass these logs and AMSI.

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell; T1059.005 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic; T1562.003 Impair Defenses: Impair Command History Logging; T1543 Create or Modify System Process; T1210 Exploitation of Remote Services

**Severity rationale:** CAT II: any vulnerability whose exploitation has a potential to result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000134**: Ensure that audit records containing information that establishes the outcome of the event.  
  Rev 5: AU-3 e · Rev 4: AU-3 · Rev 3: AU-3

### V-253416 · WN11-CC-000330 · CAT I: The Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client must not use Basic authentication.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rule ID | `SV-253416r958510_rule` |
| Severity | CAT I (high) |
| SRG | SRG-OS-000125-GPOS-00065 |
| Topic | Remote Desktop & Remote Management |
| CCI | CCI-000877 |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 5 | MA-4 c |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 4 | MA-4 c |
| NIST 800-53 Rev 3 | MA-4 c |
| Implemented via | Group Policy, Registry value |

#### Level 3: General Audience

**In plain terms:** The Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client must not use Basic authentication.

**Why it matters:** Administrators can control computers from far away, as if they were sitting at the keyboard. This rule makes sure those remote connections are encrypted, require a proper sign-in every time, and can't be used to copy files around carelessly. It's like requiring a video-verified, recorded call before anyone can give orders over the phone.

**How important is it?** High priority (CAT I): If this setting is wrong, an attacker could directly and immediately gain access, take control, or cause serious damage. These are fixed first.

**Key terms:**
- *WinRM*: A Windows service that lets administrators run commands on a computer over the network.

#### Level 2: System Administrator

**Settings changed:**

| Type | Location | Setting | Required value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WinRM\Client | AllowBasic | REG_DWORD = 0 |
| Group Policy | Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Remote Management (WinRM) >> WinRM Client | Allow Basic authentication | "Disabled" |

**How it works:** On Windows, RDP settings are under Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Remote Desktop Services >> Remote Desktop Session Host (Security / Device and Resource Redirection / Session Time Limits), and WinRM settings under Windows Components >> Windows Remote Management (WinRM Client / WinRM Service). Verify WinRM with 'winrm get winrm/config'.

**Operational impact:** Disabling drive and clipboard redirection affects admin convenience. WinRM restrictions can break management tools that use Basic auth over HTTP (some older configuration-management and monitoring products), so move those to Kerberos or HTTPS.

**Check procedure (DISA):**

```text
If the following registry value does not exist or is not configured as specified, this is a finding:

Registry Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
Registry Path: \SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WinRM\Client\

Value Name: AllowBasic

Value Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 0
```

**Fix procedure (DISA):**

```text
Configure the policy value for Computer Configuration >> Administrative Templates >> Windows Components >> Windows Remote Management (WinRM) >> WinRM Client >> "Allow Basic authentication" to "Disabled".
```

#### Level 1: Cyber Security Professional

**Vulnerability discussion (DISA):** Basic authentication uses plain text passwords that could be used to compromise a system.

**Threat & control context:** Remote-management protocols give interactive or programmatic control of a host and are a favored vector for both ransomware operators and insiders. Requirements include encrypted transport, no Basic/Digest authentication or unencrypted WinRM traffic, always prompting for credentials, no saved RDP passwords, no drive redirection, and session time limits. These implement AC-17 (remote access), AC-17(2) (confidentiality and integrity via encryption), SC-8 and AC-12 (session termination).

**MITRE ATT&CK techniques mitigated/detected:** T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol; T1021.006 Remote Services: Windows Remote Management; T1563 Remote Service Session Hijacking; T1040 Network Sniffing

**Severity rationale:** CAT I: any vulnerability whose exploitation will directly and immediately result in loss of confidentiality, availability or integrity.

**Compliance mapping:**

- **CCI-000877**: Employ strong authentication in the establishment of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions.  
  Rev 5: MA-4 c · Rev 4: MA-4 c · Rev 3: MA-4 c

---
